items.title: Hammer vs Hanging Man - 66 seconds
items.caption_top: Hammer vs Hanging Man - location decides.
items.ground_truth: FACTS ALLOWED: A hammer candle has a small body and a long lower wick, typically appearing after a decline, near support. A hanging man has the same shape but appears after a rally. Chart patterns are probabilistic, not guarantees; context (location, trend, volume) decides meaning.

script.title: Same candle, two meanings

segments.subtitle_text: Wait! Two candles with the SAME shape... one hints the market may rise, the other warns it may fall. Spot the pattern, use it... I will explain in sixty seconds.

segments.broll_prompt: Split screen of a hammer candle at a chart bottom versus the same shape at a chart top, red and green highlights
segments.subtitle_text: When you confuse a hammer with a hanging man, your entry goes wrong... you buy at the top and sell at the bottom. It is the most common mistake of new traders. Has it happened to you too? Tell the truth... how many times did you enter on the wrong candle?

segments.narration: A friend of mine kept buying hammers at market TOPS. She lost money three months straight before she showed me her chart. The trick is LOCATION. A hammer after a fall, near support... small body, long lower wick. Buyers stepped in and rejected the fall. The same shape after a rally? That is a hanging man... a WARNING, not a signal. And here is the second thing most people miss... the trend BEFORE the candle decides its meaning, not the candle alone. Volume bhi dekho. Koi bhi pattern akela guarantee nahi hai.

items.title: The stop-loss rule - 70 seconds
items.ground_truth: FACTS ALLOWED: A stop-loss is a pre-decided exit price to limit a loss. SEBI's studies have found that a large majority of individual intraday/F&O traders lose money. Discipline rules (decide max loss before the trade, exit at the planned level) are risk-management principles, not guarantees.

script.title: Decide your exit first

segments.narration: Stop-loss ko ignore karna? Bilkul nahi. Today... the ONE rule that keeps small losses small. Seventy seconds, and your next red day will feel different.
segments.subtitle_text: स्टॉप-लॉस इग्नोर करना? बिल्कुल नहीं। आज... वह एक नियम जो छोटे नुकसान को छोटा रखता है। सत्तर सेकंड, और आपका अगला लाल दिन अलग महसूस होगा।

segments.narration: Ever held a losing trade hoping it comes back? Umeed pe umeed... and suddenly a small red day became a big one. That hope is the MOST expensive emotion in trading. Sound familiar? How many times has it happened to you... twice, five times?
segments.broll_prompt: Stressed young Indian man staring at a falling red chart on his phone at night, desk lamp glow
segments.subtitle_text: कभी घाटे वाला ट्रेड यह सोचकर पकड़े रखा कि लौट आएगा? उम्मीद पर उम्मीद... और अचानक छोटा लाल दिन बड़ा बन गया। वह उम्मीद ट्रेडिंग की सबसे महंगी भावना है। जाना-पहचाना लगा? आपके साथ कितनी बार हुआ... दो बार, पांच बार?

segments.narration: मेरे एक साथी ने बिना stop-loss के एक trade में तीन दिन का profit गंवा दिया। तीन दिन की मेहनत... एक उम्मीद में खत्म। नियम सरल है: trade से पहले तय करो कि कितना खोना मंज़ूर है... aur wahi se bahar nikal jao, बिना सवाल पूछे। Doosra example... bike ka emergency brake. Brake लगाने से speed नहीं रुकती, दुर्घटना रुकती है। Stop-loss भी ऐसा ही है... wo aapko chhote loss pe rokta hai, taaki bada loss ho hi na sake.
segments.subtitle_text: A colleague of mine lost three days of profit in one trade without a stop-loss. Three days of work... gone in one hope. The rule is simple: decide before the trade how much you can afford to lose... and exit exactly there, without questions. Second example... a bike's emergency brake. The brake does not stop the speed, it stops the accident. A stop-loss is the same... it stops you at a small loss, so a big loss can never happen.

segments.narration: Stop-loss एक emergency brake है... सवारी रोकने के लिए, दुर्घटना के बाद नहीं। Decide first. Then trade. Every single time.
segments.broll_prompt: Scooter emergency brake lever close-up, then a stock chart with a red stop-loss line being respected
segments.subtitle_text: स्टॉप-लॉस एक इमरजेंसी ब्रेक है... सवारी रोकने के लिए, दुर्घटना के बाद नहीं। पहले तय करो। फिर ट्रेड करो। हर बार।

segments.narration: आपका stop-loss पहले से तय रहता है या बाद में? Comment batao... aur follow karo ek risk rule roz ke liye. Red day aaye, toh rule yaad rakhna!

items.title: What a call option is - 72 seconds
items.ground_truth: FACTS ALLOWED: A call option gives the buyer the right, not the obligation, to buy the underlying at a fixed strike price until expiry. The buyer pays a premium. Options lose value as expiry approaches (time decay). SEBI's studies have found that a large majority of individual F&O traders lose money. No specific strikes, premiums or returns may be claimed.

script.title: Option is not a lottery

segments.narration: रुको! Call option कोई lottery नहीं है... यह एक reservation टिकट है। सत्तर सेकंड दो, और expiry आपको फिर कभी surprise नहीं करेगा।
segments.subtitle_text: Wait! A call option is not a lottery... it is a reservation ticket. Give me seventy seconds, and expiry will never surprise you again.

segments.narration: ज़्यादातर लोग सिर्फ premium देखते हैं और expiry भूल जाते हैं। Cheap premium... bada sapna... aur expiry ke din account mein sirf dhuaan. आपने भी ऐसा किया है? Kitni baar option khatam hote dekha hai?
segments.broll_prompt: Confused young trader looking at an options chain with red premiums ticking down on a terminal
segments.subtitle_text: Most people only look at the premium and forget the expiry. Cheap premium... a big dream... and on expiry day, only smoke in the account. Have you done the same? How many times have you watched options expire?

segments.narration: A friend of mine bought a cheap call on Tuesday, and by Thursday... expiry had eaten it. Ab samjho asli baat: a call option gives you the RIGHT - not the duty - to buy at a fixed price till expiry. You pay a small premium for that right... like a restaurant reservation. Aur doosri baat jo koi nahi batata... time decay. Har din, har ghanta, expiry ke paas aate hi premium ki value chupke se ghat-ti hai. Theta iska naam hai. Isliye... most option BUYERS lose. SEBI ke data bhi yahi kehte hain.
segments.subtitle_text: मेरे एक दोस्त ने मंगलवार को सस्ता call खरीदा, और गुरुवार तक... expiry ने उसे खा लिया। अब असली बात समझो: call option आपको तय कीमत पर खरीदने का अधिकार देता है — मजबूरी नहीं — expiry तक। उस अधिकार के लिए छोटा सा premium देना पड़ता है... जैसे रेस्टोरेंट की reservation। और दूसरी बात जो कोई नहीं बताता... time decay। हर दिन, हर घंटे, expiry के पास आते ही premium की कीमत चुपके से घटती है। इसे theta कहते हैं। इसीलिए... ज़्यादातर option खरीदार हारते हैं। SEBI का data भी यही कहता है।

items.title: RSI, read correctly - 68 seconds
items.ground_truth: FACTS ALLOWED: RSI (Relative Strength Index) is a momentum oscillator typically read between 0 and 100; above 70 is commonly called overbought and below 30 oversold. RSI is derived from price, so it lags and is a warning, not a buy/sell signal; in strong trends it can stay overbought/oversold for long periods. No specific stock levels may be claimed.

script.title: RSI is a speedometer

segments.subtitle_text: Do you buy the moment RSI drops below 30? And the price falls further... then confusion. That is where it goes wrong... treating RSI as a signal. Happened to you? How many times did you buy oversold and watch it fall more?

items.title: The revenge-trading trap - 74 seconds
items.ground_truth: FACTS ALLOWED: Revenge trading is entering trades impulsively to recover a loss. SEBI's studies have found that a large majority of individual intraday/F&O traders lose money. The 15-minute post-loss screen break is a behavioural rule, not a profit guarantee. No specific returns may be claimed.

script.title: Losses: the 15-minute rule

segments.subtitle_text: I have seen two crashes... panic does not come to me. But revenge? That still tests me. In 74 seconds, the mistake that blows the most accounts.

PANDRAH minute ke liye screen band. Utho, paani piyo, balcony mein khade ho jao. Agla trade sirf plan se aata hai... emotion se kabhi nahi. Aur doosra niyam... ek din mein ek hi badi galti allowed hai. Uske baad din khatam. Market kal phir khulega.

And a second rule... only one big mistake allowed per day. After that, the day is over. The market will open again tomorrow.

items.title: STCG vs LTCG, simply - 76 seconds
items.ground_truth: FACTS ALLOWED (public tax law): equity shares sold within 12 months of purchase attract Short-Term Capital Gains tax at 15%. Shares held beyond 12 months attract Long-Term Capital Gains tax at 10% on gains above Rs 1.25 lakh in a financial year. Intraday/F&O income is taxed as business income, not capital gains. Always advise consulting a CA for personal cases. No other tax numbers may be claimed.

segments.narration: A retired colleague sold shares in EIGHT months and was shocked by the tax bill. Simple baat: equity ek saal ke andar bechi... Short-Term Capital Gains, 15 percent tax. Ek saal se zyada rakha... Long-Term, aur sirf Rs 1.25 LAKH se upar ke gain par 10 percent. Aur doosra example... hotel ka stay. Chhota stay, ek rate; lamba stay, doosra rate... aur ek limit ke neeche kuch comfort bhi. Intraday aur F&O ka income alag hai... wo business income maana jaata hai, capital gains nahi. Apne case ke liye hamesha CA se poocho.
